topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Data Locality
explanation: The memory hierarchy mitigates the CPU-memory performance gap by organizing storage into levels (registers, L1/L2/L3 cache, main memory) with decreasing speed and increasing capacity. Caching strategies fundamentally rely on data locality to maximize hit rates. Temporal locality dictates that recently accessed data will likely be accessed again soon, while spatial locality suggests that data near a recently accessed address will also be needed. Exploiting these properties ensures frequently required data resides in faster cache levels, minimizing average memory access time (AMAT) and boosting system throughput.
